softmax_statement: For N>0, M>=0 and every abs(u_j-v_j)<=M, sum_j abs(softmax(u)_j-softmax(v)_j)<=M. This improves the earlier checked constant 4 to 1; no optimality theorem is claimed.
proof_argument: A subset probability mass along an affine score path has derivative bounded by 2*M*p*(1-p)<=M/2. The mean value theorem bounds subset mass differences. The subset of positive endpoint differences turns twice its mass difference into the full l1 distance.
attention_hypotheses: Finite real projected query/key vectors of positive width d; epsilon>0.
A nonempty row with fixed rotary phases and fixed gain gamma.
For the joint result every raw projected key changes by Euclidean norm at most E, with E>=0.
attention_query_statement: With C=abs(gamma)*sqrt(d)/sqrt(epsilon), sum_j abs(p_j(q,K)-p_j(q2,K))<=C*norm(q-q2), improving the earlier bound 4*C.
attention_joint_statement: sum_j abs(p_j(q,K)-p_j(q2,K2))<=C*(norm(q-q2)+E), where E uniformly bounds projected-key changes before RMS. There is no extra factor N.
ssmax_specialization: gamma=m*log(N)*g. For m>=0,N>=1, C=m*log(N)*abs(g)*sqrt(d)/sqrt(epsilon). The original ideal initialization g=1/sqrt(d) cancels the width factor. The theorem also covers the actual rounded buffer gain as a real fixed scalar.
nonvacuity: Every one of the seven statements has an example. Softmax examples include a genuine two-key score change and proper subset. Attention examples use width 8, four keys, actual epsilon 1/8388608, quarter-scale SSMax ideal gain, nonzero or position-varying phases and arbitrary input vectors.
limitations: Unchanged real model; this improves the mathematical estimate, not measured behavior.
No bound on unbounded projection matrices before the projected vectors, learned phase changes, value changes, XSA or readout.
No whole-transformer conditioning, floating-point, convergence or learning theorem.
Small epsilon still permits large sensitivity constants; smaller score gain still weakens the separate concentration lower bound for a fixed margin.
Equation correspondence to PyTorch is reviewed rather than a verified translation.
preservation: All scientific Python/configurations/plans, prior proof records, short selection and active long diagnostic remain unchanged.
